paper: Mardal, Tai, Winther, SIAM J. Numer. Anal. 40(5), 1605-1631, 2002 -- A Robust Finite Element Method for Darcy-Stokes Flow

open_questions.q: Do there exist practical block-diagonal preconditioners for the MTW discretization that remain uniformly well-conditioned across the full permeability regime epsilon in [0,1], matching the epsilon-uniform stability of the discretization itself?
open_questions.basis: Section 4.2 and Theorem 5.1 establish epsilon-uniform inf-sup stability and energy-norm convergence, so the natural next question is whether the assembled saddle-point operator inherits an epsilon-uniform condition number under a block-diagonal preconditioner scaled by the H0(div)-cap-epsilon*H1 velocity norm and the L2 pressure norm. The paper does not construct or benchmark such a preconditioner; our replication measured only direct-solve wall time (~3 s at nx=32) without spectrum analysis, so uniform conditioning is not yet demonstrated for this specific 9-DOF element.
next_steps: Assemble the block-diagonal preconditioner B = diag(A_uu_scaled^{-1}, M_p^{-1}) where A_uu_scaled corresponds to the epsilon-dependent velocity energy norm.
Sweep condition number kappa(B*S) versus epsilon in {1, 2^-2, 2^-4, 2^-8, 0} and h in {2^-2, ..., 2^-6} using scipy.sparse.linalg.eigsh on the preconditioned system.
Report whether kappa remains bounded uniformly in (epsilon, h), which would upgrade the paper's approximation-theoretic result to a linear-algebra-ready statement.

open_questions.q: Is there an H(div)-conforming polynomial pair of higher order (e.g. quadratic normal moments and quadratic tangential moments) that generalizes the MTW element while preserving div V_h subset Q_h and epsilon-uniform stability, and does it deliver the expected O(h^3)/O(h^2) improvement in the smooth regime?
open_questions.basis: The paper fixes the local space at V(T) subset P_3^2 with dim=9, giving O(h^2) L^2 velocity and O(h) energy and pressure convergence. It does not discuss higher-order variants. A natural extension would use P_4 or P_5 shape functions with matching pressure space P_1 or P_2, preserving the 'just enough continuity' philosophy (paper Section 4). Whether such an extension retains the crucial property that div V(T) is contained in P_k for k = polynomial order minus 3, and whether unisolvence carries over, is not addressed.
next_steps: Repeat the paper's Lemma 4.1-style construction with P_4^2 shape space and pressure P_1: enumerate DOFs (three normal moments and two tangential moments per edge? plus interior moments?), check dim(V(T)) matches DOF count and numerical unisolvence.
If unisolvent, run the same Table 5.1 sweep and check whether observed rates are (3, 2, 2) uniformly in epsilon.
Verify div V_h subset P_1 by projecting div phi_i onto P_1 numerically.

open_questions.q: Does the MTW element extend cleanly to the full Brinkman coupling with a heterogeneous permeability tensor K(x) varying by many orders of magnitude across the domain (e.g. Darcy sub-domain adjacent to a Stokes sub-domain), and does the reproduced ±0.03-rate uniformity survive that heterogeneity?
open_questions.basis: The paper studies the constant-coefficient form (I - epsilon^2 Delta) u - grad p = f with a single scalar epsilon (Section 1). Real Brinkman applications (porous media next to free flow) have K(x) varying by 6-10 orders of magnitude across a sharp interface. Whether the epsilon-uniform stability of Theorem 5.1 becomes a K(x)-uniform stability, or degrades near sharp interfaces, is not analyzed. Our replication used only the constant-epsilon manufactured solution from the paper.
next_steps: Modify mtw_solver.py to allow a per-triangle epsilon_T = sqrt(K(x_T)), with K(x) = 1 in a subdomain and K(x) = 10^{-6} elsewhere.
Construct a manufactured Brinkman solution with an interface and compute rates versus h; check whether the interface introduces a spurious factor sqrt(K_max / K_min) in the energy error.
Compare with the interface-fitted subdomain-decomposition approach and report the ratio of errors.

open_questions.q: How does the MTW element behave on curved-boundary and unstructured (Delaunay, anisotropic-adaptive) meshes -- do the paper's rates persist, or is the negative-slope-diagonal Cartesian mesh used in Table 5.1 exploiting a hidden superconvergence?
open_questions.basis: All 20 convergence data points in the paper's Table 5.1 -- and correspondingly all 20 points in our replication -- use the same mesh family: unit square, n x n squares split by negative-slope diagonal. It is a well-known finite-element pitfall that highly regular Cartesian meshes can exhibit superconvergence that vanishes on unstructured meshes. The paper does not report unstructured or curved-domain experiments. Our replication is identically limited.
next_steps: Generate three mesh families of comparable h: (a) the paper's uniform Cartesian, (b) a Delaunay triangulation via scipy.spatial.Delaunay on Halton-sampled interior points, (c) an anisotropic mesh graded toward a boundary layer.

Rerun the Table 5.1 sweep on each mesh family and compare the fitted rates; any rate degradation below 1.8 for L^2 velocity or below 0.9 for L^2 pressure at epsilon = 1 would indicate a mesh-family artifact.
Repeat on a curved domain (e.g. quarter disc, isoparametric edge treatment for boundary triangles) and check whether the H(div) BC imposition retains machine-zero div u_h.

open_questions.q: Is the MTW saddle-point system efficiently solvable by a monolithic multigrid or a block-triangular Schur-complement solver of near-optimal complexity, or does the nonconforming/H(div) structure force a preconditioned MINRES-type approach whose cost scales worse than the standard Stokes case?
open_questions.basis: The paper is purely an approximation-theoretic contribution: stability, convergence, div-free preservation. It offers no solver algorithm. Because V_h is nonconforming and only in H(div), classical H^1-based smoothers (pointwise Gauss-Seidel) are inappropriate, and the standard multigrid theory for H(div) (Hiptmair 1997, Arnold-Falk-Winther 2000) applies to Raviart-Thomas / BDM but not directly to this element. Whether an off-the-shelf preconditioner delivers h-independent iteration counts uniformly in epsilon is unknown.
next_steps: Implement two candidate preconditioners: (i) block-diagonal MINRES with algebraic multigrid on the velocity block and mass-matrix pressure, (ii) block-triangular with an approximate Schur-complement via BFBt.
Measure iteration count and wall time versus h in {2^-2, ..., 2^-7} and epsilon in {1, 2^-4, 0}. Compare against the O(h^{-3}) cost of the direct sparse LU we currently use.
Identify the h and epsilon regime in which each preconditioner degrades and report whether uniform h-independence is achievable, thus closing the analysis-to-computation gap left open by the paper.
